chunks: Fadala ibn Sinan, from al-Sayf ibn 'Umayrah, from al-Subbah, from al-Jabir, who said: I heard a man saying to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I have two parents who are opposite (to us).' He said to him: 'Be kind to them as you are kind to the Muslims who love us.'

key_terms.بَرَّهُمَا: Be kind to them / Show filial piety
key_terms.يُوَالِينَا: They love us / Are loyal to us

ai.seo_question: How should a Shia treat non-Shia parents?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd* highlights the Shia principle that filial piety (*birr*) is not contingent upon the parents' sectarian alignment, but rather on maintaining familial bonds with the same devotion shown to loyal companions. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) instructs the man to treat his non-Shia parents with the same kindness he extends to those who follow the Ahl al-Bayt, emphasizing universal familial duty over theological conformity. This underscores the importance of *silat al-rahim* (maintaining kinship ties) as a core virtue in Shia ethics, independent of the parents' faith status.
